summary: King County, WA: a 40-foot DNR live-in tower built in 1963 was pulled down June 4, 1969 for a heliport; the last remains described date from a 1972 survey.

facts.status_note: Pulled down June 4, 1969; no source describes what stands on the summit today

access.note: Reached by old logging roads from Kent-Kangley Road; the ridge road to the true summit is closed to the public to protect the Cedar River Watershed (2020 trip report)

visit.trail_note: Logging-road hike starting on Kent-Kangley Road just south of Kangley; there is no tower to visit

events.note: New 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower; construction began August 1963. A 50-foot spar tree had been the earlier lookout on the site.
First named lookout Carol Sorensen (spelled Sorenson on Willhite's page), June 15 to Sept. 14, 1964. A 2020 trip report gives 1963 to 1969 instead.
Pulled down June 4, 1969 to make room for a heliport; vandalism cited. By March 1970 all structures were gone and the land returned to Burlington Northern, Inc.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the tower was vandalized before it could be staffed in 1964 and names Carol Sorensen as a 1964 lookout. Willhite gives her season as June 15 to Sept. 14, 1964 and records damage in fall 1963. A 2020 trip report says DNR staffed a lookout from 1963 to 1969, which the other sources do not support. The story follows the 1964 start.

The register says removed in 1969. firelookout.com says destroyed in 1969. Willhite and Forest Lookouts say pulled down or torn down on June 4, 1969 to make room for a heliport. Same event, different verbs.

notes_for_editor: Record is McDonald Mountain; Willhite's page is titled McDonald Point and firelookout.com calls it McDonald Mtn. (Point). Both describe the same 40-foot tower built in 1963 and pulled down June 4, 1969, so the story treats them as one site. Access is restricted per one 2020 WTA trip report; no official closure notice was read, so the brief's 'access: unknown' is replaced. The brief's height 12.2 m equals the 40-foot tower. Staffing start (1963 vs 1964) is disputed; the 1964 start is the one two sources support. Willhite spells the first lookout's name Sorenson, the other sources Sorensen. No photos added: the page images have no confirmed licence or direct image URL.
